niche_and_angle: Practical Claude Code automations built specifically for non-technical operations managers at B2B SaaS companies — not tutorials for developers, but working demos built by someone who has actually done the ops job and knows which 20% of automations deliver 80% of the value
platform_rationale: Ops managers and chiefs of staff at B2B SaaS companies are densely concentrated on LinkedIn. The newsletter captures the most engaged readers from LinkedIn into an owned channel. This pairing (LinkedIn for discovery, newsletter for depth and monetization) is the proven flywheel for B2B niche creators.

monetization.method: Newsletter sponsorships from B2B SaaS tools (Notion, Make.com, Loom, Airtable) at $500–$1500/issue once list exceeds 2,000 subscribers; digital product ($149 'Ops Automation Starter Pack'); 1:1 'Automation Office Hours' at $149/hr

audience_bootstrap_strategy: Week 1: Post 3 LinkedIn pieces using existing meeting summarizer content — before/after screenshots, honest reflection on building it. Tag the 2 actual users with their permission. Manually connect with 50 ops managers at 10–200 person SaaS companies. Week 2: Comment substantively on 10 posts per day from ops managers who already have audiences. Week 3–4: Guest post or newsletter swap with one adjacent newsletter in the 500–3000 subscriber range. Target: 100 email subscribers in 30 days.
north_star_metric_90_days: Email newsletter subscriber count — target 400 subscribers by day 90, with open rate above 42%
differentiation: Every other AI content creator explains what AI can do. This channel shows a real ops manager's actual workflow being automated, with real output screenshots, real edge cases, and honest failure modes. The author is not a developer cosplaying as an ops person — he has done the job for 6 years and was recently laid off, which creates a narrative tension that AI tutorial channels completely lack.

niche_and_angle: Honest, week-by-week documentation of building a consulting/product business after a tech layoff — 8-week cash runway, a father, part-time hours, and Claude Code as the primary tool. Radical specificity: actual revenue numbers, actual client conversations, actual failures, actual Claude prompts.
platform_rationale: Substack's internal discovery network has become a genuine distribution engine for personal narrative newsletters in the 'career transition' and 'building in public' categories. The format rewards long-form honesty. Supports paid subscriptions natively.

monetization.method: Paid Substack subscription at $9/month or $79/year — unlocks full weekly journal entries, the actual Claude prompts used each week, and a private Discord for others in career transition. At 12 months, add a $299 self-paced course: 'Build Your First AI Product in 30 Days on a Layoff Budget'

audience_bootstrap_strategy: Day 1: Post the 'Week 0' piece publicly on Substack and send personal messages to former colleagues — a direct ask, not a broadcast. Target 30 personal outreach messages. Day 3–7: Submit to Substack's 'Reads' curation and request recommendations from 3 complementary newsletters in the layoff/career transition/indie hacking space. Cross-post one excerpt to r/layoffs and r/cscareerquestions. Week 2–4: Comment on other Substack writers in adjacent niches. Target: 100 subscribers in 30 days.
north_star_metric_90_days: Paid subscriber conversion rate — target 8% of free subscribers converting to paid by day 90, minimum 30 paid subscribers
differentiation: The 200 other AI content creators are either developers showing off what Claude can build, or marketers explaining AI strategy. None of them are a laid-off father with 8 weeks of runway, publicly documenting real revenue numbers, real client rejections, real prompt failures, and real fear — while building actual working tools. The financial pressure, ops domain credibility, Claude Code specificity, and radical transparency create a narrative that is genuinely unreplicable.
